state.architecture:
Title: Calculator Module Update and Robustness Enhancement
Summary: Architectural design for updating and hardening the core calculator module with standard arithmetic operations, robust input validation, boundary condition management, and comprehensive unit testing to ensure deterministic results and zero regressions.
Components:
- [MODIFY] Calculator Module: Core calculation service providing standard arithmetic and utility computation methods. (Responsibilities: Execute arithmetic operations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, Validate input parameter types, bounds, and precision, Enforce defensive error handling for edge cases such as division by zero and invalid numeric inputs, Maintain backward compatibility for existing interface contracts and consumers)
- [MODIFY] Calculator Test Suite: Automated unit tests verifying operation correctness, precision, and error conditions. (Responsibilities: Provide test coverage for standard and extended calculation operations, Validate proper rejection and error raising on invalid inputs and zero division, Ensure floating-point arithmetic precision constraints are met)
Data Flow: Consumer components supply operands and operation requests to the Calculator Module. -> The Calculator Module validates input data types and values against computational constraints. -> Upon successful validation, the Calculator Module performs the computation and returns the calculated result. -> If validation fails (e.g., non-numeric input or division by zero), structured errors or designated fallbacks are returned to the caller.
Dependencies: Standard runtime mathematical operations and numeric validation utilities, Configured testing framework (e.g., Jest or Vitest) for test execution
Risks: Ambiguity in specific feature updates may lead to unnecessary modifications beyond the required calculation operations.; Altering method signatures or return types could introduce breaking changes for existing consumers.; Floating-point representation limitations in standard IEEE 754 arithmetic may cause minor precision anomalies without dedicated rounding logic.
Verification Plan: Execute baseline unit tests prior to modifications to confirm existing behavior.; Execute comprehensive test suite covering all supported operations, edge cases (zero divisor, negative numbers, large numbers), and invalid inputs.; Run static analysis, type checking, and linter validation across all modified files to ensure strict adherence to codebase standards.

Title: Calculator Module Update and Robustness Enhancement
Summary: Architectural design for updating and hardening the core calculator module with standard arithmetic operations, robust input validation, boundary condition management, and comprehensive unit testing to ensure deterministic results and zero regressions.
Components:
- [MODIFY] Calculator Module: Core calculation service providing standard arithmetic and utility computation methods. (Responsibilities: Execute arithmetic operations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, Validate input parameter types, bounds, and precision, Enforce defensive error handling for edge cases such as division by zero and invalid numeric inputs, Maintain backward compatibility for existing interface contracts and consumers)
- [MODIFY] Calculator Test Suite: Automated unit tests verifying operation correctness, precision, and error conditions. (Responsibilities: Provide test coverage for standard and extended calculation operations, Validate proper rejection and error raising on invalid inputs and zero division, Ensure floating-point arithmetic precision constraints are met)
Data Flow: Consumer components supply operands and operation requests to the Calculator Module. -> The Calculator Module validates input data types and values against computational constraints. -> Upon successful validation, the Calculator Module performs the computation and returns the calculated result. -> If validation fails (e.g., non-numeric input or division by zero), structured errors or designated fallbacks are returned to the caller.
Dependencies: Standard runtime mathematical operations and numeric validation utilities, Configured testing framework (e.g., Jest or Vitest) for test execution
Risks: Ambiguity in specific feature updates may lead to unnecessary modifications beyond the required calculation operations.; Altering method signatures or return types could introduce breaking changes for existing consumers.; Floating-point representation limitations in standard IEEE 754 arithmetic may cause minor precision anomalies without dedicated rounding logic.
Verification Plan: Execute baseline unit tests prior to modifications to confirm existing behavior.; Execute comprehensive test suite covering all supported operations, edge cases (zero divisor, negative numbers, large numbers), and invalid inputs.; Run static analysis, type checking, and linter validation across all modified files to ensure strict adherence to codebase standards.
